Long quality bar (all required)
  1. accumulation range >= 20 daily bars (climax to SOS)
  2. range width 8-40% of price
  3. clean boundaries: >= 2 touches of each edge (edge zone = 15% of the height), <= 10% of range closes outside the box
  4. a SPRING (or shakeout) that closed back inside the range: low < support - max(0.1 ATR, 0.25%), close back >= support on the break bar or within the next 3 bars, depth <= min(0.5 x range height, 15%, 3 ATR); 'shakeout' = depth >= 1.25 ATR or >= 5%
  5. a TEST of the spring 2-20 bars after the reclaim: a swing low at or above the spring low (and <= support + 0.4 x height), volume <= 0.7x the spring bar (0.7-0.8x = borderline) and a NARROWER bar (range <= 0.7x the spring bar or an inside bar; 0.7-1.0x = borderline)
  6. then an SOS bar within 30 bars of the test: volume >= 1.75x its 20-day average (the 'SOS-A' grade; the chart's SOS event needs 1.5x), range >= 1 ATR, an up close in the top third of the bar, above the range top (creek), within the first 3 bars of the jump across the creek
  7. RS >= 70
  8. liquidity: ADV50 >= $20M and price >= $5
  9. the SOS within the last 10 daily bars
  10. risk (entry to stop) <= min(8%, 3 x ATR14)

Entry: buy stop 0.1% above the SOS bar high; when a back-up / LPS exists (a swing low 3-15 bars after the SOS, >= creek - 0.25 x height, retracing <= 50% of the jump, on <= 1.0x the SOS volume) and has held 2 bars, the LPS entry is preferred: 0.1% above the LPS bar high (the card says which). Top grade 'A' = an LPS low at/above the creek within 0.1 ATR on <= 0.5x the SOS volume; other LPSs are borderline. If only the LPS levels fit the risk cap, the ticket opens at the LPS
Stop: LPS entry: below the lower of the LPS low and the SOS-bar low; SOS-breakout entry: below the SOS-bar low; minus 0.5 x ATR14 (Wilder)
Size: 0.75% of a $100,000 PLACEHOLDER account at risk (0.5% if any quality item is borderline)
Reward:risk: reward:risk to the conservative cause-effect target = (target - entry) / (entry - hard stop); shown on every ticket and flagged 'below Wyckoff's 3:1' when < 3 (Course §22M: profit should outbalance the risk by at least three to one). Flagged, not hidden
Borderline (→ 0.5%): SOS/SOW volume < 2.0x avg; width < 10% or > 35%; RS 70-74 (long) / 26-30 (short); risk > 6%; exactly 2 touches on an edge; test volume 0.7-0.8x the spring bar, test range > 0.7x the spring bar (not inside), test close < 40% of its bar or test volume > 1.0x avg20; spring/reclaim close < 50% of the bar; UT without heavy volume + weak close (short); range < 25 bars; LPS entry on a grade-B LPS (low more than 0.1 ATR under the creek, or > 0.5x the SOS volume)

Short quality bar (all required)
  1. distribution range >= 20 daily bars (climax to SOW)
  2. range width 8-40% of price
  3. clean boundaries: >= 2 touches of each edge, <= 10% of range closes outside the box
  4. an UPTHRUST / UTAD that FAILED: high > resistance + 0.1 ATR, close back <= resistance on the UT bar or within the next 2 bars, overshoot <= min(0.5 x height, 15%) (ideal: >= 1.5x volume with a close in the bottom third of the bar; otherwise borderline)
  5. then an SOW bar: volume >= 1.75x its 20-day average, range >= 1 ATR, a down close in the bottom third of the bar, below the range bottom (ice), within the first 3 bars of the drop through the ice
  6. RS <= 30
  7. liquidity: ADV50 >= $20M and price >= $5
  8. the SOW within the last 10 daily bars
  9. risk (entry to stop) <= min(8%, 3 x ATR14)

Entry: sell stop 0.1% below the SOW bar low; or 0.1% below the LPSY bar low (a swing high 3-15 bars after the SOW, <= ice + 0.25 x height, retracing <= 50% of the drop, on <= 0.6x the SOW volume) once it has held 2 bars
Stop: LPSY entry: above the higher of the LPSY high and the SOW-bar high; SOW entry: above the SOW-bar high; plus 0.5 x ATR14 (Wilder)
Size: 0.75% of a $100,000 PLACEHOLDER account at risk (0.5% if any quality item is borderline)
Reward:risk: reward:risk to the conservative cause-effect target = (target - entry) / (entry - hard stop); shown on every ticket and flagged 'below Wyckoff's 3:1' when < 3 (Course §22M: profit should outbalance the risk by at least three to one). Flagged, not hidden
Borderline (→ 0.5%): SOS/SOW volume < 2.0x avg; width < 10% or > 35%; RS 70-74 (long) / 26-30 (short); risk > 6%; exactly 2 touches on an edge; test volume 0.7-0.8x the spring bar, test range > 0.7x the spring bar (not inside), test close < 40% of its bar or test volume > 1.0x avg20; spring/reclaim close < 50% of the bar; UT without heavy volume + weak close (short); range < 25 bars; LPS entry on a grade-B LPS (low more than 0.1 ATR under the creek, or > 0.5x the SOS volume)

Trailing-stop rule (state kept day to day in feeds/wyckoff_structure/tickets.json)
  • before 1R: the hard stop is unchanged
  • at >= 1R, or once a confirmed higher low (a swing low with 2 higher-low bars after it) forms above entry: stop to breakeven or 0.1% under that higher low, whichever is higher
  • thereafter: 0.1% under each newly confirmed higher low, or under the bottom of a new trading range (re-accumulation) if one forms
  • stops only move up (longs) / down (shorts); shorts mirror with lower highs
  • status: pending -> triggered (date) -> stopped (date, R) / target hit (3R); pending not triggered within 10 bars = expired; a close through the stop before the trigger = invalidated

Method box · how ranges, events, phases, cause & effect and peers are computed

No moving averages are used anywhere on this page or in its charts. Everything is price structure + volume, following the desk notes on Weis (springs, upthrusts, effort vs result, tests), Pruden (phases, P&F count guide) and Wyckoff (climax → automatic reaction, the count). Numbers marked OURS are desk calibration: the sources publish no numeric cut-offs. Rule definitions follow research-tools/PURE_WYCKOFF_SCOPE.md (v2, source-verified).

Terminology. Spring, creek (jump across the creek), back-up (BU) and LPS/LPSY are Evans / Stock Market Institute terms, used by Pruden. Wyckoff's own Course speaks of the springboard at the bottom of a range of accumulation (§14M) and the terminal shake-out, a rapid drive down at or near the end of a period of preparation (§21M). Here "Shakeout" marks a shakeout-depth spring (the depth axis); it is the machine's label, not a claim that it is Wyckoff's terminal shake-out.

1 · Trading range from structure

  • Climax anchor. SC = a pivot low (lowest low of the prior 40 and next 5 bars) after a decline of ≥ 15% from the highest high of the prior 60 bars, with a climax bar within 2 bars that trades within 1 ATR of that low: true range ≥ 1.4× ATR20 and volume ≥ 1.8× the 50-bar average (OURS). BC mirrors it after an advance ≥ 20%.
  • AR = the automatic rally (reaction after a BC): the running extreme until price gives back ≥ 40% of it or 1 ATR, within 25 bars. Range top = AR high, bottom = SC low (BC: top = BC high, bottom = AR low). STs = later swing lows (highs) in the edge zone (35% of the height) on less volume than the climax.
  • Width 6–50% of price and ≥ 2.5 ATR; ≥ 15 bars before an exit (younger = Phase A sketch); ≤ 25% of closes outside the box. Exit older than 40 bars = stale (dropped). Weekly: 10+ weeks, 10–60% wide, 25% / 30% prior trend, stale after 20 weeks.
  • Accumulation vs distribution: prior trend (SC +1 / BC −1) plus behaviour: exit up +3 / down −3, intact spring +1.5, intact UTAD −1.5, rising swing lows +0.5, falling swing highs −0.5, up-bar vs down-bar volume ±0.5. A BC range that resolves up is re-accumulation; an SC range that resolves down is re-distribution.

2 · Events

  • Spring (PURE_WYCKOFF_SCOPE.md §1.2): a low below support by more than max(0.1 ATR, 0.25%), with a close back ≥ support on the break bar or within the next 3 bars (weekly 2), depth ≤ min(0.5× the range height, 15%, 3 ATR); only once the range is ≥ 15 bars old (earlier = ST). Shakeout = a deep spring (≥ 1.25 ATR or ≥ 5% under support); the volume class (high-volume ≥ 1.5× avg20, no-supply ≤ 1.0× with a ≤ 1 ATR bar) and the best close location of the spring/reclaim bar are recorded separately. Repeated probes are one episode until price moves 25% of the height away; the episode keeps its lowest low. A later close below the spring low marks it broken.
  • Test: a swing low 2–20 bars after the reclaim (weekly 2–10), at or above the spring low and in the lower 40% of the range, on ≤ 0.8× the spring bar's volume and on a narrower bar (true range below the spring bar's, or an inside bar). Ticket grade: ≤ 0.7× volume and ≤ 0.7× range (or inside).
  • UT / UTAD: a high above resistance by more than 0.1 ATR that closes back ≤ resistance on the same bar or within the next 2 bars (weekly 2; an upthrust "immediately reacts"), overshoot ≤ min(0.5× height, 15%); UTAD once the range is ≥ 20 bars old (weekly 10). The UT/UTAD label is by age only: in a range that resolves as (re-)accumulation it is simply a late upthrust inside the cause, not a distribution signal.
  • SOS (jump across the creek): a close above the top not reclaimed within 2 bars; the SOS bar is the heaviest bar of the jump (consecutive higher closes above the creek) with volume ≥ 1.5× avg20, true range ≥ 1.0 ATR20 and an up close in the top third of the bar (else "Breakout"). ≥ 1.75× = SOS-A (ticket grade). BU / LPS: a swing low 3–15 bars after the SOS, ≥ creek − 0.25× height, retracing ≤ 50% of the jump, on ≤ 1.0× the SOS bar's volume. Grade A (top LPS) = a low at/above the creek within 0.1 ATR on ≤ 0.5× the SOS volume; otherwise grade B (borderline). Labelled BU when the low comes to rest on the creek (creek − 0.1 ATR to creek + 0.15× height), else LPS. LPSY: ≤ ice + 0.25× height on ≤ 0.6× the SOW volume. Failed breakout: a close below creek − 0.25× height within 10 bars (or below mid-range later): the range resumes. SOW / LPSY / failed breakdown mirror these. News gap: an open ≥ 1 range height beyond the far edge from a close near the range ends the structure (no SOS/SOW, no ticket).
  • Phases: A = climax, AR, until the first ST · B = building cause · C = spring / UTAD (+ test) · D = SOS + LPS (SOW + LPSY), or a rally into the top quarter ≥ 5 bars after the spring · E = markup / markdown (a close ≥ 0.5× the height beyond the edge, ≥ 5 bars after the exit or ≥ 1× the height at once). Recent = last 10 daily bars (4 weekly).

3 · Cause & effect

  • Horizontal point-and-figure count on closes across the range, from the left wall (climax) to the count line. Box = half the mean true range of the range, rounded to a nice step (1 / 2 / 2.5 / 5 × 10ⁿ) and clamped to 12–40 boxes across the range height; 3-box reversal. Count = columns × box × 3.
  • Accumulation: count line = LPS, else test, else spring, else the support line. Aggressive = count line + count; conservative = the spring low (or range low) + count (Pruden's count guide: add the count to the exact low or between low and count line).
  • Distribution: count line = LPSY, else the resistance line; aggressive = count line − count; conservative = the UT/UTAD high (or range high) − count.
  • Range-height projection: top + height (bottom − height). The row shows conservative = the nearer of the P&F conservative count and the projection, aggressive = the farther of the P&F aggressive count and the projection. Counts are "points to stop, look and listen", not forecasts.

4 · Structural peers

  • Same timeframe, side and phase; similarity = 100·exp(−d²/2) with d² = (ln width ratio / 0.35)² + (ln duration ratio / 0.45)² + (ln P&F columns ratio / 0.45)². Top 5 with score ≥ 20.

5 · Universe and data

  • RS-ranked liquid list (2,714 names) → desk liquidity floor (50-session average daily dollar volume (close x volume) >= $20M and price >= $5) → 2,042 scanned. Massive grouped-daily adjusted bars (RS cache, no API calls); weekly = Yahoo 10y history spliced with Massive (springs_history.tf_bars). No API calls.
  • Code: research-tools/wyckoff_structure.py → feeds/wyckoff_structure/latest.json, tickets.json; page research-tools/wyckoff_structure_page.py; daily via run_all.sh (mode structure).

Caveats

  • Ranges need a climactic anchor: quiet re-accumulation bases without a climax are not detected. Daily history is ~16 months (Massive cache), so the oldest daily ranges are truncated at the chart's left edge. Weekly rows use Yahoo history spliced with Massive. Chart payloads ship ~160 daily bars for names outside the covered set, so long ranges can start off-chart. Machine labels are a first read: Weis warns schematics become "cookie prints"; check the chart.

Research, not advice. Machine-read Wyckoff structure on daily (and weekly) bars as of Mon 5 Oct 2026; levels and counts are for study, not recommendations. Trade tickets size a $100,000 PLACEHOLDER account. Short tickets require shorting / inverse capability. Generated 2026-10-06 15:30 AEST by research-tools/wyckoff_structure_page.py.
